clue.text: Agitator from East London ready to follow revolutionary brief

indicators.note: the money piece comes after the rearranged letters
something revolutionary turns everything over, so the letters of brief are rearranged

parts.note: ready is slang for cash; East London is a city in South Africa, whose currency is the rand

explanation.surface: A troublemaker from London's East End who is quick to take up a radical's instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: East London here is not the Cockney East End but the South African city, so its ready money is the rand. 'revolutionary' rearranges BRIEF into FIREB.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a synonym for a rabble-rouser who stirs up unrest.

clue.text: Joy of life after moving to Dublin, perhaps

indicators.note: once its letters have been moved about, life becomes a new arrangement

parts.note: Dublin is an example of a capital city

explanation.surface: Someone finds the joy of life after relocating to Ireland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after moving' reads like relocating abroad, but it is the signal to shuffle the four letters before Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is a formal synonym for happiness or bliss.

clue.text: Copier — one office has it stored away?

definitions.text: Copier — one office has it stored away?

indicators.note: the letters sit tucked inside the run of words copier, one, office, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A duplicating machine that one office keeps in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The machine name runs across 'copieR ONE Office'; the whole clue also describes the old stencil duplicator an office might keep in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: Roneo was a trade name for a stencil duplicating machine, a forerunner of the photocopier.

clue.text: How often we get inspiration — and the rest

definitions.meaning: read cryptically as ..., the rate at which we inhale
a pause or respite from activity

explanation.surface: A question about creative inspiration, followed by everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' is taken literally as drawing breath, so the first part splits as BREATHING'S PACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathing space is a short respite, a pause that lets someone recover.

clue.text: Insistent girl should meet male model

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a male is a man
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A demanding girl insists on being introduced to a male fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' is not a fashion model but Ford's Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone unshakeably firm, refusing to be moved from a position.

clue.text: "Lost taxi turns up in river" fiasco

indicators.note: the cab and lost pieces are placed inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a taxi is a cab
L is the abbreviation for lost in league tables

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a missing taxi found in a river, a real fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses CAB to BAC; with L it goes into DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure, a synonym for a complete shambles.

clue.text: A Monty Python sketch, originally funny

definitions.text: A Monty Python sketch, originally funny

indicators.note: funny suggests these opening letters are set out in an odd order
originally points to the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A comment that a particular Monty Python sketch was funny in its first form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes A, M, P, S; 'funny' rearranges them. The whole clue names the famous canned-meat sketch in which diners are offered little else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spam sketch is a well-known Monty Python routine set in a cafe where every dish includes canned luncheon meat.

clue.text: Composer using piano, so the French one

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
ergo is Latin for therefore, so
les is a French word for the, in the plural
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer writing for piano, and so the French one, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: Pergolesi was an Italian Baroque composer, famous for his Stabat Mater.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Pergolesi was an eighteenth-century Italian composer, an example of the category.

clue.text: The majority on vacation yearn for North Welsh port

parts.note: the majority means most

indicators.note: with its interior vacated, yearn keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Most people on holiday long for a trip to a little harbour in North Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties YEARN to YN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mostyn is a small harbour town on the Dee estuary in Flintshire, North Wales.

clue.text: Port model ordered

parts.note: Bristol is a port city in the west of England
to model something is to fashion it

explanation.surface: A model of a port arranged neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from 'shipshape and Bristol fashion', a sailors' saying from the busy port.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol fashion is an idiom meaning neat, in good order, as a well-kept ship would be.

clue.text: Cut corner heading into narrow street

indicators.note: the picked letter is placed inside the street

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or street

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone cuts the corner by heading into a narrow side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut corner' reads as a driving shortcut; 'Cut' alone is the verb, as a doctor cuts a boil.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to pierce or cut open with a blade, as a surgeon does with an abscess.

clue.text: Light grey French perfume ingredient

parts.note: amber is a traffic light
gris is French for grey

explanation.surface: A pale grey French scent component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light grey' reads as one colour but splits: the amber traffic light, then the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales, long used as a fixative in fine perfumery.

clue.text: Busy actor turned sloth? Split evident here

indicators.note: a busy actor rushes about, so the letters of actor are jumbled
turned means the animal's name is read backwards

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: A hard-working actor becomes lazy, and a split in the cast is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is not a rift but the Adriatic city. 'Busy' shuffles the actor into a Balkan nationality; 'turned' flips the crossword's favourite sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is a port city on the Dalmatian coast, so this country is where it can be seen.

clue.text: Keeping like a sweet sauce, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: something resembling custard could be called custardy

explanation.surface: Something kept like a sweet sauce, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, custardy and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Custody is the safekeeping or guardianship of a person or thing.

clue.text: Dish of boiled hen — it's fed to a wild dog in India

indicators.note: being fed into something means going inside it

parts.note: the dhole is an Asian wild dog

indicators.note: boiled suggests ingredients churned up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it is the thing fed in

explanation.surface: A recipe: boil a hen, then feed it to a wild dog in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiled' shuffles the bird and the pronoun, which are 'fed' into the dog. Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad-in-the-hole is a traditional British dish, an example of a meal of sausages in Yorkshire pudding batter.

clue.text: Right inside the bar, no drunk is offensive

indicators.note: the right piece goes inside the rearranged letters
drunk suggests the letters are reeling about

explanation.surface: Being drunk inside a bar, right there, is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' shuffles eight letters, and 'inside' slips the abbreviation for right into the middle of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means detestable, so offensive in the strongest sense.

clue.text: Cause pain to Irish horse, say — one mounted the night before

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means placed upwards, so these pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
a means one
eve is the evening before an event

explanation.surface: Upsetting an Irish horse by riding it the night before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns the first three pieces upward together, as a down light reads; the evening follows unturned.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to distress or wrong someone, inflicting hurt feelings.

clue.text: Set of steps needed for tossing the caber?

definitions.meaning: a dance is a set of steps
the caber toss happens at Scottish games; a throw is a fling, and the setting is upland

explanation.surface: A question about what footwork a caber tosser needs.
explanation.walkthrough: The caber toss is a Scottish games event where a tree trunk is thrown end over end; the second half reads as a mountain throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a traditional Scottish solo dance, an example of a set of steps.

clue.text: Vegetation that's fine in a gale moving east

indicators.note: the fine piece is placed within the other letters
moving means the letters of a gale are shifted around

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Plants thriving in a gale blowing eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges A GALE into LEAAG; E follows and 'in' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is a collective word for foliage, the leaves of plants.

clue.text: Uninterrupted playing of pontoon's lacking nought

indicators.note: playing a game shuffles the cards, so the remaining letters are reordered
lacking means one letter is missing

parts.note: the card game's name plus the s
O is nought, zero

explanation.surface: A marathon session of pontoon in which no one scores zero.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for blackjack. Removing an O leaves PONTONS, and 'playing of' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means continuing without a break, so without interruption.

clue.text: Container one Geordie home put out for recycling?

definitions.text: Container one Geordie home put out for recycling?

indicators.note: the clue's first word has some letters put out and the rest recycled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Geordies come from Newcastle in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A Newcastle household puts its packaging out for the recycling collection.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word doubles as fodder: 'put out' removes one and the Geordie's home region, leaving CONTAR for 'recycling' to rearrange. A Geordie is someone from Tyneside.
explanation.definitionFit: A carton is a cardboard box, an example of packaging that goes in household recycling.

clue.text: Sound advice daughter ignored, in general

indicators.note: Sound signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: remove D (daughter) from advice to leave a vice, and a vice is a gripper

explanation.surface: Good advice that a daughter ignored, given by a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound advice' looks like wise counsel; 'Sound' is the homophone signal. A vice grips, and in non-rhotic speech 'a gripper' matches the Roman general's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a Roman general, Augustus's chief commander at Actium.

clue.text: Wine drunk by loveless fiddle player is more disgusting

indicators.note: the wine goes into the player, as a drink is taken in
love is zero in tennis, so the O is dropped

parts.note: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Wine drunk by a fiddler who has lost love is all the more unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' strips the zero from the emperor, leaving NER, and 'drunk by' takes the Italian wine inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier is the comparative of nasty, meaning more unpleasant or revolting.

clue.text: National Rail quick? No luck there, sadly

indicators.note: No says the letters of the following word are not in the result
sadly suggests the remaining letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A rail traveller laments that fast trains bring no luck there.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LUCK from RAIL QUICK to leave RAIQI, which 'sadly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a citizen of Iraq, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Number I love to sing about opening of railway cutting

indicators.note: the number goes around the railway's first letter

parts.note: I is one and love is zero in tennis, so together they write 10

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A favourite song gets sung around the opening of a new railway cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number I love' looks like a favourite song; I and O written together make 10. 'railway cutting' hides the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive, sharp and forceful, as a cutting remark is.

clue.text: Mad as an animal that is trapped

indicators.note: the animal is caught between the two letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: As mad as a trapped animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' here means angry, not crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means furious, and mad is an informal synonym for angry.

clue.text: Fanatical followers of Brazil and Barcelona?

definitions.meaning: words that come after Brazil and Barcelona, as in Brazil ... and Barcelona ..., a kind of hazelnut

explanation.surface: Passionate football fans of Brazil and Barcelona.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: the followers are the edible kind, Brazil nuts and Barcelona hazelnuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nuts about something means being crazy for it, so fanatical.

clue.text: Former writer's holding stationery items dear

indicators.note: the first pieces enclose the stationery items

parts.note: ex means former
the writer says I have, shortened to I've
pens are items of stationery

explanation.surface: A former writer keeps hold of their stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's' is the setter speaking of themself: I've, from I have.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly is a synonym for high-priced.
